title: Merged Möbius and rational steps lose the formula's signed zeros, so the chain takes the other side of the formula's own cut
detail: Expr.compile evaluates −u with CX.neg, c − u with CX.sub and u/c with CX.div. These keep or flip the sign of a zero imaginary part, and log, √ and powers read that sign on their cut. The reader replaces them with catalog steps. A neg becomes mul(c = −1+0i), and (−1)·(x+0i) gives +0. u/c becomes mul(1/c). Constants from the exact rational normal form have +0 imaginary parts. So, at points where the formula's argument lands exactly on a branch cut, the chain takes the limit from the other side. The commonest case is a neg feeding straight into log, √ or a power. There, ordinary inputs with +0 imaginary part, such as the real axis, already differ. For √(−z²) and log(−z²) this is the whole real axis. For (−z)^{i} the values differ by a factor e^{2π}, not by a sign. Forward-mapped curves such as Im z = 0, probes or tour points at real z, and a y = 0 pixel row or mesh row would be drawn on the other side of the cut. t_recognize has exact axis points with ±0, but its corpus has no neg or merged constant directly in front of a branch function (only e^{−z}), so it does not see this. Values off the cut lines agree: 180 shared-number cases and 4,192 fuzzed formula and cut pairs, at generic and ±1e-9 points, give no mismatch except math-2 to math-4.
evidence: node notes/formula-recognition/tools/review_math_repro.js (math-1). Cut 180, formula versus chain: \log(-z) at 1+0i: −πi vs +πi. \sqrt{-z} at 2.5+0i: −1.581i vs +1.581i. (-z)^{i} at 1+0i: 23.1407 vs 0.0432. \sqrt{-z^2} at −2+0i (every real z): −2i vs +2i. \log(-z^2) at 0.5+0i: −1.386−πi vs −1.386+πi. \sqrt{-1-z} at 2: −1.732i vs +1.732i. \sqrt{-(z-1)} at 2: −i vs +i. \log(-\frac{z}{2}) at 2: −πi vs +πi. With −0 inputs: \log(\frac{z}{2}) at −2−0i: +πi vs −πi; \sqrt{2z-1} and \sqrt{(z+(-1))+z} at −2−0i: −2.236i vs +2.236i. Inverse trig is not affected: \arcsin(-z), \arccos(-z), \arctan(-z) and \operatorname{artanh}(-z) match on the axes.
fix: Give each merged Möbius-type run, and each rational part, a CPU f that replays the formula's own subtree for that run: Expr.compile of the run with its input as z, on the same θ. Keep the catalog vals for the GPU plan, the inverse ops, the path and the lamps. Then CPU values, curves and probes are the formula's, bit for bit. The alternative is a global choice: make CX.neg (and constant folding) give canonical +0 (0 − x). That removes most cases on both sides, but it changes the formula's own on-cut values (see math-7). Add to t_recognize: \log(-z), \sqrt{-z}, \sqrt{-z^2}, (-z)^{i}, \sqrt{-1-z}, \log(\frac{z}{2}) and \sqrt{2z-1}, at (x, +0) and (x, −0).

title: Cut angles outside (−180°, 180°] are normalised in finish(), which is not bit-identical to Expr's argCut(θ) on the cut ray
detail: recChain passes the formula's cut in degrees to the steps. Funcs.finish then rewrites it as (cut − 360m, sheet k + m). The formula evaluates argCut(a, θ) with the raw θ. (a) Cut −180 or 540: θ ≠ Math.PI, so the formula closes its interval at the ray for both signed zeros. The chain's step has cut 180, which takes the principal atan2, and that returns −π for −0. Adding 2πk then lands on the wrong end, so the chain gives the other sheet on the negative real axis with −0. Inner steps such as neg, conj or a root can produce such points. (b) Cut 270 versus −90, and 360 versus 0: θ and the normalised angle are not exactly 2πm apart in doubles. The formula's own argCut also misplaces points within about 1e-16 rad of the ray (cut 360: arg 1e-17 becomes 2π). Over an inner map that saturates onto the ray, such as z/z ≈ 1+1e-17i or cot w → −i, this covers an open set. No case was found at cuts −120, 45, 90 or 180.
evidence: review_math_repro.js (math-2). Formula versus chain. \log z, cut −180, at −2−0i: ln2 − πi vs ln2 − 3πi. \sqrt{z}, cut −180, at −2−0i: −1.414i vs +1.414i. z^{i}, cut −180, at −2−0i: 17.80+14.79i vs 9532+7918i. \sqrt{z}, cut 540, at −2−0i: −1.414i vs +1.414i. \sqrt[3]{\frac{z}{z}}, cut 360, at a generic point: e^{2πi/3} vs 1 (everywhere). \sqrt{\cot(\sin(z)\cos(z))}, cut 270, at −1.9490−2.2990i: −0.707+0.707i vs 0.707−0.707i. Fuzz: \sin(\sqrt[3]{\sqrt{z}}) and 3-\operatorname{artanh}(z^{2.5}) at cuts −180 and 540, at −0 axis points.
fix: Evaluate the chain's log, root and powa steps with the formula's raw θ. For example, keep the user's cut un-normalised in the vals of a recognized step, or give these steps' f a theta override equal to cut·DEG. Then the CPU values call argCut exactly as Expr.compile does, and the GPU and inverse code can keep the normalised (cut, k). Add t_recognize cases at cuts −180, 270, 360 and 540, with ±0 axis points and a saturating inner map.

title: Spine Möbius merging fills removable points and lights lamps the formula does not have; ∞ intermediates turn into NaN
detail: The rule that a removable point is never filled in is only enforced through Inverse.rationalForm (rf.removed). In the spine, consecutive Möbius factors are multiplied into one matrix. When an inversion is undone by a later one, the formula's pole disappears. The formula evaluates 1/(1/0) as 1/(∞+∞i) = NaN, but the chain is finite there. asChain then ORs the chain's lamps into the formula's, so for example sin(1/(1/z)) shows 'entire'. The reverse also happens. A merged 'mobius' step evaluates (0·u + b)/(u + 0) with mobApply, and an affine step evaluates −1·u + b. These give NaN when u = ∞, where the formula's b/u or b − u gives 0 or a finite limit, for example at the branch points of artanh. Both directions affect isolated points only.
evidence: review_math_repro.js (math-3), all at z = 0, formula versus chain. \sin(\frac{1}{\frac{1}{z}}): NaN vs 0, and the lamps gain 'entire' (formula alone: analytic only). \sqrt{\frac{1}{\frac{1}{z}}}: NaN vs 0. e^{\frac{1}{1/z+1}}: NaN vs 1. At z = −1: \operatorname{arsinh}(\frac{2-i}{\operatorname{artanh}(z)}): −0−0i vs NaN; \coth((2-i)-\operatorname{artanh}(z)): 1 vs NaN.
fix: When a run is merged, pull each factor's pole back to the run's input. If one of those poles is not a pole of the merged matrix, keep that run as a formula part, or refuse, as rationalForm does with removed. For the ∞ direction, either accept and document it (isolated points), or use the replayed CPU f from math-1, which fixes both directions.

title: Entire-function identities evaluate finite values where the formula, as written, overflows to NaN (and once the reverse)
detail: sin u / cos u → tan u, e^A e^B → e^{A+B} and the cosh/sinh/cos/sin readings are exact identities. The formula's own arithmetic overflows earlier: for example, Inf/Inf in sin/cos when |Im u| > ~710. So the chain draws finite, correct values where today's picture has NaN holes. With a large inner map this happens in an ordinary window: tan(e^z) for Re z > ~6.6 on the CPU, and earlier in float32 on the GPU. In one case the chain overflows where the formula does not: ½ sin 2u versus sin u cos u at |Im u| ≈ 710. This departs from 'the same values everywhere', but towards the true function.
evidence: review_math_repro.js (math-4), formula versus chain. \frac{\sin(e^{z})}{\cos(e^{z})} at 7+i: NaN vs i. e^{3z}e^{-2z} at 240+0.5i: ∞+NaN·i vs 1.49e104+8.15e103i. \frac{e^{iz}-e^{-iz}}{2i} at 0.3+720i: NaN vs ∞. \sin(z)\cos(z) at 0.4+710i: ∞+NaN·i vs NaN.
fix: This is a policy call. Either accept it and record it in DESIGN §1 (identities may be defined where the spelled formula overflows; t_recognize already skips non-finite formula values), or refuse these identity readings when an inner step is unbounded (exp, a power, a pole). Accepting looks right.

title: A shared number still decides the structure: inside a two-operand node, rationalForm reads z^{a} at the current a, and Möbius naming depends on the value
detail: power() makes any exponent that holds a shared number powa at every value. But multi() calls Inverse.rationalForm, which reads the exponent's current value. An integer a makes the node rational (Möbius, Joukowski, poly or rational), and a non-integer a leaves it unrecognized. nameMob also names the merged matrix by value: identity is dropped, then mul, add, affine, recip or mobius. Values are right at every a: 180 checks of 15 formulas at 12 values of a, including sign changes, a = 0 and a = e, found no mismatch. The step list does change, and with it the natural path (the equal sub-intervals jump), the lamps, the cuts, the GPU key (a recompile) and exact versus forward rendering. That is the user's original z^{a} complaint again, now inside a quotient or product, and DESIGN §1 says the shared number never decides the structure.
evidence: review_math_repro.js (math-5). \frac{z^{a}}{z+1}: a=−1 rational; a=0,1 mobius; a=2 add>joukowski>affine; a=2.5 not recognized; a=3 rational. z^{a}z: pown at a=1,2,3; not recognized at a=−1, 0, 2.5. z^{a}+z: joukowski>mul / add / mul / poly / none / poly. e^{z+a}: exp at a=0, add>exp otherwise. GPU key [['exp']] vs [['add'],['exp']]. \frac{az+1}{z+a}: recip at a=0, mobius otherwise (keys differ); refused at a=±1, as intended.
fix: In multi(), skip the rational normal form, or treat the node as not rational, when any pow exponent or root index in the subtree hasParam. It then reads the same at every a: a formula part, or the identities. For Möbius runs that contain a shared number, keep one generic step type (affine or mobius) at every value, and do not drop the identity. Then the key and the path kind stay fixed while a is dragged. Add t_recognize cases that sweep a across integers and 0 and check that the chain signature stays the same.

title: The rational normal form reads decimal literals as exact decimals, but the formula evaluates binary doubles, so cancellation can change the degree and the lamps
detail: Inverse.rationalForm's exact stage takes a literal like 0.3 as 3/10, while Expr.compile uses the nearest double. Values always agree to within about 1e-16 of the terms' sizes. The REC_PROBES guard also refused the large-cancellation cases tried, such as z+1/((0.1+0.2−0.3)·10^{16}z+1). But when the decimal cancellation is exact, the structure comes from the exact reading. For (0.1+0.2−0.3)z³+2z the chain is mul(2), with the lamps injective, Möbius and degree 1. The function actually evaluated is 5.55e-17·z³ + 2z, which is not injective, and whose value at 1e8 is 2.555e8 against the chain's 2e8. The same happens with a shared number near a literal: (a−0.7)z² + z at a = 0.7+1e-13 gives a coefficient of 1.0000e-13 against the formula's 1.0003e-13. The RAT_SNAP zeroing of noise coefficients for non-literal constants (π, e, √2, shared numbers) has the same effect. Both are pre-existing in customOps; now they also decide paths and lamps.
evidence: review_math_repro.js (math-6). (0.1+0.2-0.3)z^3+2z → mul, lamps entire, mobius, proper, injective, deg=1 (formula alone: deg=3?). At 1e8: 255511151.23 vs 200000000. (0.1+0.2-0.3)z^2+z+1 → add, lamps injective, deg 1; at 1e8: 100000001.555 vs 100000001.
fix: Choose a policy. Either accept it, since the exact reading is what the user typed, and say so in DESIGN. Or build the exact parts from the doubles that Expr.compile uses, not from the decimal strings, so the normal form describes the evaluated function. In either case, do not claim injective or Möbius from a degree that dropped through cancellation of inexact or decimal constants.

title: Pre-existing in Expr, not the recognizer: negative constants carry −0 imaginary parts, so 'principal' constant values are on the wrong sheet
detail: −1 parses as neg(1) = −1 − 0i, and CX.log and powReal read atan2(−0, −1) = −π. So the constant √(−1) is −i, log(−1) is −πi, (−8)^{1/3} is 1 − 1.732i, and (−1)^z is e^{−iπz}. The code comment in Expr.compile says constants take their principal value. The recognizer copies Expr exactly (cval uses Expr.compile), so there is no mismatch. If Expr is fixed, the recognizer follows. The root cause is the same CX.neg −0 as in math-1, so fixing it would also change which side math-1's formulas take on their cuts.
fix: A separate decision for Expr (it changes saved formulas' values on cuts): canonicalise −0 to +0 in constant folding (or compute neg as 0 − x). Decide it together with math-1.
